notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 728 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 89 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 120 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 731 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 731 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 89 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 120 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 658 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 120 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 60 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Compare the constant operand form with its variable operand counterpart.
notes.investigate: Review the constant-operation cost model. Multiplication helpers in constant division/remainder are consistent with reciprocal-multiply expansion; check intermediate IR before attributing the cause.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Both sources mask variable shift counts to the operand width minus one.
notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 28 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 28 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 2 fewer source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.

notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 120 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 180 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 612 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 105 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 60 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Compare the constant operand form with its variable operand counterpart.
notes.investigate: Review the constant-operation cost model. Multiplication helpers in constant division/remainder are consistent with reciprocal-multiply expansion; check intermediate IR before attributing the cause.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 27 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 27 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 8 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

    ld a, b

    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec bc
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr nz, .copy
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

memmove::
    push bc
    ld d, c
    ld e, b
    ld c, a
    ld hl, sp + 4
    ld b, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 5
    ld a, [hli]
    ld h, [hl]
    ld l, a
    push bc
    push hl
    pop bc
    pop hl
    ld a, e
    sub l
    ld a, d
    sbc h
    jr c, .forward
    add hl, bc
    ld a, e
    add c
    ld e, a
    ld a, d
    adc b
    ld d, a
.backward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
    dec bc
    jr .backward
.forward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
.copy:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec bc
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr nz, .copy
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c
    ret

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

.done:

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

memmove::
    push bc
    ld d, c
    ld e, b
    ld c, a
    ld hl, sp + 4
    ld b, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 5
    ld a, [hli]
    ld h, [hl]
    ld l, a
    push bc
    push hl
    pop bc
    pop hl
    ld a, e
    sub l
    ld a, d
    sbc h
    jr c, .forward
    add hl, bc
    ld a, e
    add c
    ld e, a
    ld a, d
    adc b
    ld d, a
.backward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
    dec bc
    jr .backward
.forward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
.copy:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec bc
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr nz, .copy
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c
    ret

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

memmove::
    push bc

    ld hl, sp + 4
    ld b, [hl]

    ld a, [hli]
    ld h, [hl]
    ld l, a
    push bc
    push hl
    pop bc
    pop hl
    ld a, e
    sub l
    ld a, d
    sbc h
    jr c, .forward
    add hl, bc
    ld a, e
    add c
    ld e, a
    ld a, d
    adc b
    ld d, a
.backward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
    dec bc
    jr .backward
.forward:
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr z, .done
.copy:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec bc
    ld a, b
    or c
    jr nz, .copy
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c
    ret

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 222 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 36 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 56 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.

Sangoku has 42 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 40 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 483 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 52 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 80 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

notes.investigate: These totals exclude further runtime helpers. Compare caller frames and callee prologues independently.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 837 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 60 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 240 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 2568 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 334 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 480 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

notes.investigate: These patterns include locals, stack arguments and caller/callee saves. Register-allocation dumps or liveness analysis are required to classify exact spills; this is not peak stack depth.

notes.observation: The deliberately non-inlined fixture callees are measured separately from the caller.
notes.investigate: These totals exclude further runtime helpers. Compare caller frames and callee prologues independently.

notes.observation: Compare the same computation with an inline/no-call control.
notes.investigate: The delta includes call marshaling, preservation and changed scheduling, not just proven spill instructions.

Sangoku has 605 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 960 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1625 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1625 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 241 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1761 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1761 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 286 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 180 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u32_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint32_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint32_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

; Context: a[L], b[L], op, status. Ops: 0 udiv, 1 urem, 2 sdiv, 3 srem,

; divisor and 2 is signed division overflow. Every register is clobbered.
; Frame: 0..31 scratch, 32 L, 33 op, 34 context, 36 sign a, 37 sign b,
; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF

.mul_copy

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1390 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1390 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 205 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 44 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u64_decimal_derived(uint8_t *dst, uint64_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint64_t q = value / 10; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value - q * 10); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

; BC = context: a (8 bytes), b (8 bytes), op, status. Result replaces a.
__gbc_wide64::

    ld e, b
    ld a, 8

; In: DE = context, A = operand length L in bytes (8 or 16).
; Context: a[L], b[L], op, status. Ops: 0 udiv, 1 urem, 2 sdiv, 3 srem,
; 4 umulhi, 5 smulhi, 6 imul. The result replaces a. Status 1 is a zero
; divisor and 2 is signed division overflow. Every register is clobbered.
; Frame: 0..31 scratch, 32 L, 33 op, 34 context, 36 sign a, 37 sign b,
; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF
    ld hl, sp + \1
    ld c, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
IF \2 == 0
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
ENDC
    ld a, c
    and a
    call nz, __gbc_wide_neg
ENDM

Sangoku has 169 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 52 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

'0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

; Shift or rotate the 8-byte little-endian value at BC in place. Byte 8 holds
; the op (0 shl, 1 ushr, 2 sshr, 3 rotl, 4 rotr) and byte 9 the count,
; taken modulo 64. Every register is clobbered.

    ld e, b
    ld hl, 8
    add hl, de
    ld a, [hli]
    ld b, a
    ld a, [hl]
    and 63
    ld c, a
    ret z
.loop
    call __gbc_wshift_bit64
    dec c
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1877 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 269 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 280 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t spans_tokenize_loop(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, const uint8_t *set) { uint16_t i = 0, count = 0; while (src[i]) { uint16_t j = 0; while (set[j] && set[j] != src[i]) ++j; if (set[j]) { ++i; continue; } uint16_t start = i; do { ++i; j = 0; while (set[j] && set[j] != src[i]) ++j; } while (src[i] && !set[j]); dst[2 * count] = (uint8_t)start; dst[2 * count + 1] = (uint8_t)(i - start); ++count; } return count; }

Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 60 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.

notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 731 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 89 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 120 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 120 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1190 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 200 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 140 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 100 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Both sources mask variable shift counts to the operand width minus one.
notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

Sangoku has 36 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Both sources mask variable shift counts to the operand width minus one.
notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 140 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 188 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 188 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 36 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Both sources mask variable shift counts to the operand width minus one.
notes.investigate: Inspect shift-count widening, repeated masks and helper argument setup; unsafe unchecked shifts are not being compared against wrapping shifts.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 28 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 28 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 2 fewer source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Compare this lowering with the next smaller integer width.
notes.investigate: Inspect carry/sign propagation and live multi-byte values. The growth also includes wider arguments/results.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

    ld d, c
    ld e, b
    ld c, a
    ld hl, sp + 4
    ld b, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 5
    ld a, [hli]
    ld h, [hl]
    ld l, a
    push bc
    push hl
    pop bc
    pop hl
.forward:
    srl b
    rr c
    jr nc, .skip_one
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.skip_one:
    srl b
    rr c
    inc b
    inc c
    jr nc, .test
    jr .copy_two
.copy_four:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.copy_two:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.test:
    dec c
    jr nz, .copy_four
    dec b
    jr nz, .copy_four
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c
    ret

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

Sangoku has 8 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 38 bytes larger than SDCC.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 38 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.

    srl b

    srl b

    srl b

    ld a, [hli]

    dec c

    pop bc

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

    ld a, e

    ld e, a
    ld a, d
    adc b
    ld d, a
.backward:
    srl b
    rr c
    jr nc, .back_skip_one
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
.back_skip_one:
    srl b
    rr c
    inc b
    inc c
    jr nc, .back_test
    jr .back_copy_two
.back_copy_four:
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
.back_copy_two:
    dec hl
    dec de
    ld a, [hl]
    ld [de], a
    dec hl

    ld a, [hl]

.back_test:
    dec c
    jr nz, .back_copy_four
    dec b
    jr nz, .back_copy_four
    jr .done
.forward:
    srl b
    rr c
    jr nc, .skip_one
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.skip_one:
    srl b
    rr c
    inc b
    inc c
    jr nc, .test
    jr .copy_two
.copy_four:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.copy_two:
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
.test:
    dec c
    jr nz, .copy_four
    dec b
    jr nz, .copy_four
.done:
    pop bc
    ld a, b
    ld b, c
    ret

Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

cases.domain: valid pointers and readable/writable ranges within single allocations; lengths and string lengths <= 32766; no address wrapping; copy ranges do not overlap unless memmove; NUL-terminated strings for unbounded scans
