notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

The length is known at compile time.

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 37 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 12 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers reverses the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: copy includes original destination pointer return; overlap allowed only for memmove
The length is known at compile time.
notes.investigate: Check whether a small inline copy/fill/compare beats passing a constant count to a general routine; measure cycles separately.

support_functions.c_function: NOINLINE uint32_t fixture_leaf_u32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return (uint32_t)(a + b); }

cases.semantic_note: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 800 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 800 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 47 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

sangoku.measurement_note: source patterns only; leading add-sp reservation excludes pushes, return addresses and alternate frame setup; adjacent stack accesses are lower bounds, not proven spill counts or peak depth

sdcc.measurement_note: source patterns only; leading add-sp reservation excludes pushes, return addresses and alternate frame setup; adjacent stack accesses are lower bounds, not proven spill counts or peak depth

notes.investigate: These patterns include locals, stack arguments and caller/callee saves. Register-allocation dumps or liveness analysis are required to classify exact spills; this is not peak stack depth.

notes.observation: The deliberately non-inlined fixture callees are measured separately from the caller.
notes.investigate: These totals exclude further runtime helpers. Compare caller frames and callee prologues independently.

notes.observation: Compare the same computation with an inline/no-call control.
notes.investigate: The delta includes call marshaling, preservation and changed scheduling, not just proven spill instructions.

analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1330 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 196 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 240 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

sangoku.measurement_note: source patterns only; leading add-sp reservation excludes pushes, return addresses and alternate frame setup; adjacent stack accesses are lower bounds, not proven spill counts or peak depth

sdcc.measurement_note: source patterns only; leading add-sp reservation excludes pushes, return addresses and alternate frame setup; adjacent stack accesses are lower bounds, not proven spill counts or peak depth

notes.investigate: These patterns include locals, stack arguments and caller/callee saves. Register-allocation dumps or liveness analysis are required to classify exact spills; this is not peak stack depth.

notes.observation: The deliberately non-inlined fixture callees are measured separately from the caller.
notes.investigate: These totals exclude further runtime helpers. Compare caller frames and callee prologues independently.

notes.observation: Compare the same computation with an inline/no-call control.
notes.investigate: The delta includes call marshaling, preservation and changed scheduling, not just proven spill instructions.

Sangoku has 187 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 360 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: matching pressure control with the leaf arithmetic written inline; scheduling may differ because there is no call clobber

support_functions.c_function: NOINLINE uint64_t fixture_leaf_u64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { return (uint64_t)(a + b); }

Sangoku has 605 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 960 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: volatile loads occur before the call; dependent nonlinear folding uses each value afterward and prevents a simple reduction before the call
Compare explicit stack reservation and adjacent stack load/store patterns.

support_functions.c_function: NOINLINE uint64_t fixture_touch_u64(uint8_t *p, uint64_t a) { p[0] ^= (uint8_t)a; p[7] = (uint8_t)(p[7] + 1u); return (uint64_t)p[7]; }

notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_decimal_derived(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value / 10; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value - q * 10); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

library.measurement: isolated linked reachable ELF ROM sections; no startup or entry harness; section padding included

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1666 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1666 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 258 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 160 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: NUL-terminated output; count excludes NUL; temporary is fully initialized before reads; separate div/mod and derived remainder forms expose quotient reuse

evidence.domain: valid non-overlapping allocations unless overlap is explicit; lengths <= 128; NUL strings fit their allocations; output buffers have at least 256 bytes; unsigned arithmetic wraps; parse library variants exclude overflow

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u16_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint16_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint16_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

analysis.summary: Sangoku function body is 1790 bytes larger than SDCC.
analysis.metric: static function-body bytes; reachable dependency size reported separately when available

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1790 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 290 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 180 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: NUL-terminated output; count excludes NUL; temporary is fully initialized before reads; separate div/mod and derived remainder forms expose quotient reuse

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u32_decimal_derived(uint8_t *dst, uint32_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint32_t q = value / 10; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value - q * 10); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1744 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 283 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 180 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u32_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint32_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint32_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 20 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

sections.name: 64-bit divide and multiply
sections.assembly:
; BC = context: a (8 bytes), b (8 bytes), op, status. Result replaces a.
__gbc_wide64::
    ld d, c
    ld e, b
    ld a, 8
    jp __gbc_wide_core

sections.name: wide divide and multiply core
sections.assembly:
; In: DE = context, A = operand length L in bytes (8 or 16).
; Context: a[L], b[L], op, status. Ops: 0 udiv, 1 urem, 2 sdiv, 3 srem,
; 4 umulhi, 5 smulhi, 6 imul. The result replaces a. Status 1 is a zero
; divisor and 2 is signed division overflow. Every register is clobbered.
; Frame: 0..31 scratch, 32 L, 33 op, 34 context, 36 sign a, 37 sign b,
; 38 bit counter, 39 temporary.

MACRO NEG_IF
    ld hl, sp + \1
    ld c, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
IF \2 == 0
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
ENDC
    ld a, c
    and a
    call nz, __gbc_wide_neg
ENDM

__gbc_wide_core::
    add sp, -40
    ld hl, sp + 32
    ld [hli], a
    inc hl
    ld [hl], e
    inc hl
    ld [hl], d
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [hl], 0
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld [hl], a
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld [hl], 0
    inc hl
    ld [hl], 0
    cp 4
    jp nc, .mul
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    xor a
.zero_check
    or [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .zero_check
    and a
    ld c, 1
    jp z, .fail
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld a, [hl]
    bit 1, a
    jr z, .unsigned
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    call __gbc_wide_sign
    ld hl, sp + 37
    ld [hl], a
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
    call __gbc_wide_sign
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld [hl], a
    NEG_IF 36, 0
    NEG_IF 37, 1
.unsigned
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld a, b
    add a
    add a
    add a
    ld hl, sp + 38
    ld [hl], a
    ld hl, sp + 0
    xor a
.clear
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .clear
.bit
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld c, b
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
    and a
    call __gbc_wide_shl1
    ld a, 0
    rla
    ld hl, sp + 0
    ld b, c
    rra
    call __gbc_wide_shl1
    ld a, 0
    rla
    ld hl, sp + 39
    ld [hl], a
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld d, h
    ld e, l
    ld hl, sp + 0
    call __gbc_wide_sub
    ld a, 0
    rla
    xor 1
    ld hl, sp + 39
    or [hl]
    ld [hl], a
    jr nz, .take
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld d, h
    ld e, l
    ld hl, sp + 0
    call __gbc_wide_add
.take
    ld hl, sp + 39
    ld c, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld a, [de]
    or c
    ld [de], a
    ld hl, sp + 38
    dec [hl]
    jp nz, .bit
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld a, [hl]
    and 1
    jr z, .quotient
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld hl, sp + 0
    call __gbc_wide_copy
.quotient
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld c, [hl]
    bit 1, c
    jr z, .done
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld a, [hli]
    ld b, [hl]
    bit 0, c
    jr nz, .sign_ready
    xor b
.sign_ready
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld [hl], a
    NEG_IF 36, 0
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld a, [hl]
    cp 2
    jr nz, .done
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld a, [hl]
    and a
    jr nz, .done
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
    call __gbc_wide_sign
    and a
    jr z, .done
    ld c, 2
.fail
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld e, b
    ld d, 0
    add hl, de
    inc hl
    ld [hl], c
.done
    add sp, 40
    ret

.mul
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld c, b
    ld d, h
    ld e, l
    ld hl, sp + 0
.copy_b
    ld a, [de]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .copy_b
    ld b, c
    xor a
.clear_high
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .clear_high
    ld a, c
    add a
    add a
    add a
    ld hl, sp + 38
    ld [hl], a
.mul_bit
    ld hl, sp + 0
    ld a, [hl]
    rra
    ld a, 0
    jr nc, .shift
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    call __gbc_wide_high
    call __gbc_wide_add
    ld a, 0
    rla
.shift
    ld hl, sp + 32
    ld b, [hl]
    call __gbc_wide_shr_product
    ld hl, sp + 38
    dec [hl]
    jr nz, .mul_bit
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld a, [hl]
    cp 5
    jr nz, .mul_result
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld h, d
    ld l, e
    call __gbc_wide_sign
    and a
    jr z, .after_a
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld d, h
    ld e, l
    call __gbc_wide_high
    call __gbc_wide_sub
.after_a
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    call __gbc_wide_sign
    and a
    jr z, .mul_result
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    call __gbc_wide_high
    call __gbc_wide_sub
.mul_result
    call __gbc_wide_ctx
    ld hl, sp + 33
    ld a, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 0
    cp 6
    jr z, .mul_copy
    call __gbc_wide_high
.mul_copy
    call __gbc_wide_copy
    add sp, 40
    ret

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a

MACRO NEG_IF

; Out: DE = a, HL = b, B = L. Keeps C. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_ctx:
    ld hl, sp + 36
    ld e, [hl]
    inc hl
    ld d, [hl]
    ld hl, sp + 34
    ld b, [hl]
    ld h, 0
    ld l, b
    add hl, de
    ret

; Out: HL = scratch + L, B = L. Only valid one call deep.
__gbc_wide_high:
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    ld b, c
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Out: A = 1 when negative, else 0.
__gbc_wide_sign:
    ld c, b
    ld b, 0
    add hl, bc
    dec hl
    ld a, [hl]
    rlca
    and 1
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L, carry in. Out: carry.
__gbc_wide_shl1:
.loop
    rl [hl]
    inc hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst += src; out: carry.
__gbc_wide_add:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    adc [hl]
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = dst, DE = src, B = L. dst -= src; out: carry is borrow.
__gbc_wide_sub:
    and a
.loop
    ld a, [de]
    ld c, a
    ld a, [hl]
    sbc c
    ld [hli], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = array, B = L. Two's complement negate.
__gbc_wide_neg:
    scf
.loop
    ld a, [hl]
    cpl
    adc 0
    ld [hli], a
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: HL = src, DE = dst, B = L.
__gbc_wide_copy:
.loop
    ld a, [hli]
    ld [de], a
    inc de
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

; In: B = L, A = carry bit. Shifts the 2L byte product right one bit.
__gbc_wide_shr_product:
    ld c, a
    ld a, b
    add a
    ld b, a
    ld hl, sp + 2
    ld d, 0
    ld e, b
    add hl, de
    dec hl
    ld a, c
    rra
.loop
    rr [hl]
    dec hl
    dec b
    jr nz, .loop
    ret

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 1051 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 169 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 52 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t format_u64_hex(uint8_t *dst, uint64_t value) { uint8_t tmp[20], i = 0; do { uint64_t q = value >> 4; uint8_t d = (uint8_t)(value & 15); tmp[i++] = (uint8_t)(d < 10 ? '0' + d : 'a' + d - 10); value = q; } while (value); for (uint8_t j = 0; j < i; ++j) dst[j] = tmp[i - 1 - j]; dst[i] = 0; return i; }

    ld a, [hli]
    ld b, a
    ld a, [hl]
    and 63
    ret z
    srl a

    jr z, .bits

    dec c
    jr nz, .byte_loop

    add hl, de
    ld a, [hl]
    and 7
    ret z
    ld c, a

    dec c
    jr nz, .bit_loop

Sangoku has 74 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 343 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 31 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 20 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: optional 0x prefix; unsigned wrapping accumulator; no digits means offset zero

notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t spans_strtok_library(uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, const uint8_t *set) { strcpy((char *)dst, (const char *)src); uint16_t count = 0; char *token = strtok((char *)dst, (const char *)set); while (token) { ++count; token = strtok(NULL, (const char *)set); } return count; }

notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

cases.c_function: uint16_t search_binary_loop(const uint16_t *src, uint16_t n, uint16_t value) { uint16_t low = 0, high = n; while (low < high) { uint16_t mid = low + (high - low) / 2; if (src[mid] < value) low = mid + 1; else if (src[mid] > value) high = mid; else return mid; } return UINT16_MAX; }

Sangoku has 40 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: strictly increasing keys avoid unspecified duplicate-match choices; generic callback cost differs from monomorphized Rust comparison

cases.c_function: uint8_t * search_insertion_sort(uint16_t *dst, uint16_t n) { for (uint16_t i = 1; i < n; ++i) { uint16_t value = dst[i], j = i; while (j && dst[j - 1] > value) { dst[j] = dst[j - 1]; --j; } dst[j] = value; } return (uint8_t *)dst; }

notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: Sangoku function body is 278 bytes larger than SDCC.
Sangoku has 47 more source instructions referencing SP.
notes.investigate: Inspect value lifetimes, stack slot reuse and argument/result marshaling. SP references include arguments and locals, so they are not a pure spill count.

notes.observation: The source uses different amounts of native register-pair arithmetic.
notes.investigate: Compare native 16-bit address arithmetic with split-byte add/carry sequences. Account for differing algorithms and calling conventions before attributing the size gap.

notes.observation: The emitted source has different branch structure.
notes.investigate: Inspect compare/boolean lowering and fallthrough layout; branch counts alone do not determine cycles.

notes.observation: Sangoku emits register self-copies or an immediate reload of a value just copied from that register.
notes.investigate: Add or improve post-allocation copy cleanup; verify register liveness before removing the original copy.

notes.observation: 20 bytes are emitted through db. They count toward function size but are absent from source mnemonic counts.
Part of the implementation is outside the measured function body.
notes.investigate: Compare reachable helper bodies and calling conventions before judging total code size or speed.

notes.observation: The wrappers use different helper calls or tail transfers.
notes.investigate: A tail transfer can avoid a call/return pair and argument cleanup in the wrapper. An inline loop versus a helper trades shared code size against call overhead; measure runtime before choosing.

notes.observation: Including reachable helpers preserves the function-body ranking.
notes.investigate: This is cold, isolated ROM cost. Shared helpers are charged once per case; an application can amortize them across calls. SDCC cost is at archive-member granularity.

notes.observation: same state transitions and wrapping decimal accumulator; shared exits and loop-carried state
